dedupe_keys.name: daily emergency ambulance dispatches temperature and air pollution in a medium sized german city 2011 2019

description: This daily series counts emergency ambulance dispatches in a medium-sized German city over nine years, alongside temperature and air pollution, to measure how heat and polluted air raise demand for emergency medical services. The producers are Philipp Schneider, Annegret Thieken and Ariane Walz of the University of Potsdam, who deposited the data and R script for their time series analysis. Coverage is 1 January 2011 to 31 December 2019, one row per day. Columns give counts of ambulance and fire service dispatches, split by cause such as non-traumatic, traumatic, cardiovascular, respiratory, injury and traffic; daily mean, maximum and minimum temperature; heatwave indicators at several percentile thresholds; and mean, maximum and minimum ozone, fine particles and nitrogen dioxide. The file is available as a free download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: the city is not named in the deposit, only aggregate daily counts are given, and the column meanings rely on the script and article. Simulation uses: estimating how heatwaves increase ambulance demand for climate adaptation planning, and forecasting daily emergency service workload from weather forecasts. Related records: the RKI emergency department surveillance data (data-rki-emergency-department-surveillance) include heat-related visits, and the Ambulance Victoria statistics (data-ambulance-victoria-incident-statistics) give another ambulance demand record.
